cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because jsonNode is null
cases.description: Verify that getSchema throws a NullPointerException when both arguments are null. The method delegates to newJsonSchema which expects a non‑null schema node.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because jsonNode is null
cases.description: When only the JsonNode argument is null the factory should reject the call regardless of a provided configuration.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) with default configuration applied
cases.description: If the configuration argument is null the factory must fall back to its internal default SchemaValidatorsConfig while still creating a schema from the supplied empty JSON object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose internal schemaNode equals the supplied node and whose validators config equals defaultConfig
cases.description: Happy‑path test: a minimal valid JSON schema and a default configuration should produce a usable JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) with customConfig applied (e.g., typeLoose flag true) and containing the complex schema structure
cases.description: Ensures that a non‑default SchemaValidatorsConfig is correctly propagated to the created JsonSchema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose internal schemaNode is a NullNode
cases.description: A JSON schema that is the literal `null` is still a valid schema according to the specification; the factory should accept a NullNode.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) with an array schema node
cases.description: Validate that the factory can handle a top‑level array node (used for schema combinators like anyOf) without throwing.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance whose effective config has typeLoose = false
cases.description: Confirm that the config supplied to getSchema is not altered internally; the resulting schema must reflect the exact settings of configA.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance whose effective config has typeLoose = true
cases.description: Same as previous case but with a different flag value, ensuring the factory does not cache or reuse a previous configuration.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose internal schemaNode is a BooleanNode representing true
cases.description: A JSON Schema can be the boolean literal true which means any instance is valid. The factory should accept a BooleanNode and return a JsonSchema without throwing.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose internal schemaNode is a BooleanNode representing false
cases.description: A JSON Schema can be the boolean literal false which means no instance is valid. The factory should accept a BooleanNode and return a JsonSchema without throwing.

input.value: textNode (JsonNode representing a JSON string "some text")

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose internal schemaNode is a TextNode
cases.description: Although a TextNode is not a valid schema according to the spec, the factory method does not perform validation at creation time; it should still wrap the node in a JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) created with internal default SchemaValidatorsConfig and the supplied integer schema
cases.description: When the configuration argument is null the factory must fall back to its internal default configuration while still correctly handling a non‑empty schema node.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose effective config has typeLoose=true, format validation disabled, and failFast=true
cases.description: Ensures that a complex SchemaValidatorsConfig with several flags is fully propagated to the created JsonSchema.

cases.expected: First JsonSchema instance reflects typeLoose=false; second call with same config after first call still reflects typeLoose=false (no mutation)
cases.description: Pass the same SchemaValidatorsConfig instance to two successive getSchema calls and verify that the factory does not mutate the config between calls.

cases.expected: Second JsonSchema instance also reflects typeLoose=false
cases.description: Continuation of the previous scenario: the second schema creation must see the unchanged configuration.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) whose meta‑schema is Draft‑07 (as indicated by $schema) and whose internal schemaNode matches the supplied node
cases.description: When the supplied schema contains a $schema keyword, the factory should load the corresponding meta‑schema and associate it with the created JsonSchema.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because the factory attempts to treat a MissingNode as a concrete schema node
cases.description: When the supplied JsonNode is a MissingNode (represents a non‑existent value), newJsonSchema cannot determine a schema location and throws NPE.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because the $schema URI does not map to a known meta‑schema
cases.description: The factory should reject schemas that declare an unknown meta‑schema identifier, raising an IllegalArgumentException during meta‑schema loading.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or URISyntaxException wrapped in IllegalArgumentException) thrown because the $schema value is not a valid URI
cases.description: A malformed URI in the $schema keyword should cause the factory to fail while trying to resolve the meta‑schema.

input.value: configWithNullMap (SchemaValidatorsConfig whose internal map field is explicitly set to null)

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because the factory expects a non‑null configuration map when propagating flags
cases.description: If a custom SchemaValidatorsConfig instance has its internal map cleared (null), the factory should detect the invalid state and raise an exception rather than proceeding with a null map.

group: Null JsonNode with Non‑Null Config (explicit check)

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown because jsonNode is null irrespective of a provided configuration
cases.description: Even when a non‑null configuration is supplied, a null JsonNode must cause an NPE; this case verifies that the config does not mask the null‑node check.
